title: Keep a conversation going
goal: Keep a simple conversation alive with follow-up questions, quick reactions and turn-taking, and make a plan together.

items.en: agreeing: me too (after a yes sentence) / me neither (after a no sentence)

drills.prompt: “J'aime le café.” You like coffee too. You say:
drills.explain: Positive sentence + you agree → Moi aussi.

drills.prompt: “Je ne parle pas chinois.” You don't speak Chinese either. You say:
drills.explain: Negative sentence + you agree → Moi non plus.

drills.text: — Je n'ai pas de voiture. — Moi non ___.
drills.en: I don't have a car. — Me neither.
drills.explain: After a negative sentence, “me neither” is moi non plus.

items.en: Tell me (all about it)! (to a friend)

accept: Est-ce que cette place est libre ?

blocks.title: A conversation café in Montréal
blocks.context: Amira arrives at a French conversation café and sits next to Nguyen. Notice how they react and keep asking questions.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Bonjour ! Cette place est libre ?
lines.en: Hello! Is this seat free?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Oui, bien sûr ! Je m'appelle Nguyen.
lines.en: Yes, of course! My name is Nguyen.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Enchantée. Moi, c'est Amira. Tu habites à Montréal ?
lines.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Amira. Do you live in Montréal?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Oui, à Rosemont. Et toi ?
lines.en: Yes, in Rosemont. And you?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Moi aussi, j'habite à Rosemont !
lines.en: I live in Rosemont too!

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Ah bon ? Super ! Tu fais quoi dans la vie ?
lines.en: Oh really? Great! What do you do for a living?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Je suis infirmière. Je travaille à l'hôpital, la nuit.
lines.en: I'm a nurse. I work at the hospital, at night.

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: La nuit ? C'est difficile, non ?
lines.en: At night? That's hard, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Oui, un peu, mais j'adore mon travail. Et toi ?
lines.en: Yes, a little, but I love my job. And you?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Je suis étudiant en informatique. Mais je ne parle pas très bien français.
lines.en: I'm a computer science student. But I don't speak French very well.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Moi non plus ! Mais on apprend. Pourquoi est-ce que tu apprends le français ?
lines.en: Me neither! But we're learning. Why are you learning French?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Parce que je veux travailler à Montréal après mes études. Et toi ?
lines.en: Because I want to work in Montréal after my studies. And you?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Je dois passer un examen de français pour mon travail.
lines.en: I have to take a French exam for my job.

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: C'est vrai ? C'est quand ?
lines.en: Really? When is it?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Le mois prochain. Alors dimanche, je vais étudier toute la journée !
lines.en: Next month. So on Sunday I'm going to study all day!

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Bon courage ! Moi, ce week-end, je vais faire du vélo. Tu veux faire du vélo avec moi samedi ?
lines.en: Good luck! This weekend I'm going cycling. Do you want to go cycling with me on Saturday?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Oui, je veux bien ! Samedi matin ?
lines.en: Yes, I'd love to! Saturday morning?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Samedi à dix heures, devant le métro, c'est correct ?
lines.en: Saturday at ten, in front of the metro, is that okay?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Oui, c'est correct ! Envoie-moi un texto. Mon numéro, c'est le 514 555 0163.
lines.en: Yes, that's fine! Send me a text. My number is 514 555 0163.

blocks.body: Count how many times each person **asks a question back**. That's the secret: nobody just answers and stops.

steps.title: Keeping the ball in the air

blocks.title: Answer, add, ask back
blocks.body:
A conversation is like a ball game: when the ball comes to you, send it back. A good answer has three parts:

1. **Answer** the question: [[Oui, à Rosemont.]]
2. **Add one detail**: [[C'est près du métro.]]
3. **Ask back**: [[Et toi ?]] / [[Et vous ?]] or a new question: [[Tu habites où ?]]

With this simple rule, even a short A1 answer keeps the conversation going.

blocks.title: Quick reactions
head: Reaction
English
Use it when…
rows: you hear something new or a little surprising
you're surprised and want to hear more
it's big news: a new job, a baby, an exam
blocks.note: Your voice matters: [[Ah bon ?]] and [[C'est vrai ?]] go **up** at the end, like a question. [[Super !]] and [[Dommage !]] go **down**.

blocks.title: Me too, me neither
head: They say…
You agree
You disagree
blocks.note: Look at the sentence you hear: **positive** → [[moi aussi]]; **negative** (*ne… pas*) → [[moi non plus]]. [[Si]] is a special “yes” that contradicts a negative: [[Tu n'aimes pas le café ? — Si !]] (Yes, I do!)

blocks.title: Follow-up questions
blocks.note: Reuse the question words from lesson 1 to ask for more. Short questions are perfect in conversation: [[Où ça ?]] [[Quand ça ?]] [[Avec qui ?]] [[Pourquoi ?]] [[C'est comment ?]] (What's it like?)

examples.fr: Je vais à Vancouver. — Ah bon ? Quand ça ?
examples.en: I'm going to Vancouver. — Oh really? When?

examples.fr: J'ai un nouveau travail. — Félicitations ! C'est où ?
examples.en: I have a new job. — Congratulations! Where is it?

examples.fr: Je fais du yoga. — C'est vrai ? C'est comment ?
examples.en: I do yoga. — Really? What's it like?

examples.fr: Je ne peux pas samedi. — Dommage ! Et dimanche ?
examples.en: I can't on Saturday. — Too bad! And Sunday?

blocks.title: Taking turns
blocks.body:
- **Give the turn:** [[Et toi ?]] (friend) / [[Et vous ?]] (formal). Stay consistent: don't mix *tu* and *vous* with the same person.
- **Gain a little time:** [[Euh…]] [[Bon…]] [[Alors…]] French speakers use them all the time; they're much better than silence or *umm*.
- **Check you understood:** [[Pardon ?]] [[Tu peux répéter ?]] [[Comment ça ?]] (What do you mean?)
- **Finish politely:** [[Bon, je dois y aller. À bientôt !]] (Well, I have to go. See you soon!)

- **Moi aussi after a negative:** *Je n'aime pas le froid. — Moi aussi* sounds like “I like it too”. Say [[Moi non plus.]]
- **Not *moi aussi pas*:** the negative “me neither” is always [[moi non plus]].
- **Ah bon, not ah bien.** [[Ah bon ?]] is a fixed expression.
- **Yes/no-only answers stop the conversation.** [[Oui.]] → [[Oui, j'adore ça ! Et toi ?]]
- **Don't translate “How was it?” here:** you don't know the past tense yet. Use [[C'est comment ?]] for things that are still happening.

Reactions you will hear in Québec:

- [[Allô !]] = hi! (in person too, not just on the phone)
- [[Pas pire !]] = literally “not worse”, it means **pretty good**: [[Ça va ? — Pas pire, toi ?]]
- [[C'est correct.]] = it's okay, that's fine.
- [[Voyons donc !]] = No way! / Come on! (surprise or disbelief)
- [[C'est le fun !]] = it's fun, it's great.

Recognize them all; [[Pas pire]] and [[C'est correct]] are safe to use yourself.

examples.fr: Allô ! Ça va ? — Pas pire, toi ?
examples.en: Hi! How are you? — Pretty good, you?

examples.fr: Je vais faire du ski à Tremblant ! — C'est le fun !
examples.en: I'm going skiing at Tremblant! — That's great!

blocks.title: Safe small-talk topics
blocks.body:
With people you don't know well in Canada, easy topics are: **the weather** ([[Il fait froid, hein ?]]), weekend plans, where you live, your neighbourhood, sports and hobbies, and where you're from.

Avoid asking about salary, rent, age or religion in a first conversation. And a last tip: [[hein ?]] at the end of a sentence (like “eh?”) invites the other person to agree: [[Il fait beau, hein ?]]

blocks.title: React with your voice
blocks.note: The melody is half the meaning. Copy the voice going up or down.

lines.fr: Ah bon ?
lines.en: Oh really?

lines.fr: C'est vrai ?
lines.en: Is that true?

lines.fr: Super !
lines.en: Great!

lines.fr: Moi non plus.
lines.en: Me neither.
lines.tip: The s of plus is silent here.

lines.fr: Dommage ! Et dimanche ?
lines.en: Too bad! And Sunday?

lines.fr: Bon, je dois y aller. À bientôt !
lines.en: Well, I have to go. See you soon!

blocks.fr: Je ne mange pas de viande. — Moi non plus.
blocks.en: I don't eat meat. — Me neither.
blocks.prompt: Does the second person eat meat?
blocks.explain: [[Moi non plus]] agrees with a negative: the second person doesn't eat meat either.

blocks.fr: J'ai un nouveau travail ! — C'est vrai ? Félicitations !
blocks.en: I have a new job! — Really? Congratulations!

steps.title: Unit checkpoint
steps.intro: This checkpoint mixes the whole unit with earlier ones. Answer without scrolling back.

blocks.prompt: Your friend says “Je n'aime pas le hockey.” You don't like hockey either. You say:
optionFeedback: Moi aussi agrees with a positive sentence.
Pas moi disagrees with a positive sentence.
Moi, si ! means you DO like it.

blocks.prompt: A colleague says “Je vais avoir un bébé !” The best reaction:
optionFeedback: Moi non plus answers a negative sentence.
Correct French, but much too cold for big news!

blocks.text: — Je vais à Québec ce week-end. — Ah bon ? Tu vas faire ___ là-bas ?
blocks.en: I'm going to Québec City this weekend. — Oh really? What are you going to do there?
blocks.explain: At the end of an informal question, “what” is quoi.

blocks.prompt: We have two children. And you? (formal)
accept: Nous avons deux enfants. Et vous ?
On a deux enfants. Et vous ?
blocks.explain: avoir: nous avons / on a. Formal “and you?” = Et vous ?

blocks.prompt: What are you going to do tonight? (to a friend)
accept: Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire ce soir ?
Tu vas faire quoi ce soir ?
Ce soir, tu vas faire quoi ?
Ce soir, qu'est-ce que tu vas faire ?
Ce soir tu vas faire quoi ?
Ce soir qu'est-ce que tu vas faire ?
blocks.explain: Near future: tu vas + faire. Any of the three question registers is fine.

blocks.text: Je me ___ à six heures parce que je ___ travailler à sept heures.
blocks.en: I get up at six because I have to work at seven.
blocks.explain: se lever → je me lève (accent è); devoir → je dois + infinitive.

blocks.prompt: Do you want some coffee? (to a friend)
blocks.explain: tu veux + partitive du (de + le) café.

blocks.fr: Je préfère le thé, mais ma femme préfère le café.
blocks.en: I prefer tea, but my wife prefers coffee.
blocks.explain: [[ma femme préfère le café]] = my wife prefers coffee.

blocks.fr: Il fait froid aujourd'hui, mais demain il va faire beau.
accept: Il fait froid aujourd'hui mais demain il va faire beau.
blocks.explain: Present for today ([[il fait froid]]), near future for tomorrow ([[il va faire beau]]).

blocks.prompt: Match each reaction to its meaning.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.intro: This is your unit mission. Use everything from units 1 to 10.

blocks.prompt: Imagine a 60-second conversation with a new neighbour in the elevator and play both people. Person A asks questions; person B answers, adds a detail, reacts and asks back. End by making a plan together.
checklist: At least four questions with different question words
Two reactions (Ah bon ?, C'est vrai ?, Super !…)
Moi aussi or moi non plus
A suggestion with tu veux… ? or vous voulez… ?

models.label: Model conversation
models.fr:
— Bonjour ! Vous habitez ici ?
— Oui, au troisième étage. Je m'appelle Raj. Et vous ?
— Moi, c'est Lucie. Vous êtes d'où, Raj ?
— Je suis indien, mais j'habite à Ottawa maintenant. Je travaille dans une banque.
— Ah bon ? Moi aussi, je travaille dans une banque !
— C'est vrai ? Super ! Et vous aimez le quartier ?
— Oui, mais je n'aime pas l'hiver ici.
— Moi non plus ! Il fait très froid. Qu'est-ce que vous allez faire ce week-end ?
— Je vais aller au marché samedi matin. Vous voulez venir avec moi ?
— Oui, je veux bien ! À quelle heure ?
— À dix heures, devant l'immeuble ?
— Parfait. À samedi !
models.en:
— Hello! Do you live here?
— Yes, on the third floor. My name is Raj. And you?
— I'm Lucie. Where are you from, Raj?
— I'm Indian, but I live in Ottawa now. I work in a bank.
— Oh really? I work in a bank too!
— Really? Great! And do you like the neighbourhood?
— Yes, but I don't like the winter here.
— Me neither! It's very cold. What are you going to do this weekend?
— I'm going to go to the market on Saturday morning. Do you want to come with me?
— Yes, I'd love to! What time?
— At ten, in front of the building?
— Perfect. See you Saturday!

blocks.prompt: Write a text-message exchange of 6 to 8 short messages between you and a friend. Make a plan for the weekend: what, when, where, and one problem (someone can't, or has to do something).
checklist: At least three question words (où, quand, quel…)
A clear plan at the end: day, time, place

models.label: Model exchange
models.fr:
Mei : Salut Karim ! Tu fais quoi samedi ?
Karim : Salut ! Je dois travailler le matin. Pourquoi ?
Mei : Je vais faire un pique-nique au parc avec Sofia. Tu veux manger avec nous ?
Karim : Super idée ! Mais je ne peux pas avant deux heures.
Mei : Pas de problème. À quelle heure tu finis ?
Karim : À une heure et demie. On se retrouve où ?
Mei : Devant la bibliothèque, à deux heures et quart ?
Karim : C'est correct ! Je vais apporter des fruits. À samedi !
models.en:
Mei: Hi Karim! What are you doing on Saturday?
Karim: Hi! I have to work in the morning. Why?
Mei: I'm going to have a picnic in the park with Sofia. Do you want to eat with us?
Karim: Great idea! But I can't before two.
Mei: No problem. What time do you finish?
Karim: At half past one. Where shall we meet?
Mei: In front of the library, at quarter past two?
Karim: That works! I'm going to bring some fruit. See you Saturday!

summary:
- Keep a conversation going: answer, add a detail, ask back with [[Et toi ?]] / [[Et vous ?]]
- React naturally: [[Ah bon ?]] [[C'est vrai ?]] [[Super !]] [[Dommage !]] and agree with [[moi aussi]] / [[moi non plus]]
- Ask follow-up questions and make a plan together with [[tu veux… ?]], [[je peux / je dois]] and [[aller + infinitif]]
